To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cell-free expression system can be used to express the native Hc proteins of the most important botulinum toxins.
the Hc fragments of botulinum neurotoxin A, B, or E were produced in a cell-free system, purified, and formulated into an alum-adsorbed vaccine that protected mice against botulinum toxin challenge.

a cell-free expression platform was used for the production of recombinant Hcs of botulinum A, B, or E toxins and that immunization with these vaccines induced protection against a toxin challenge in mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of recombinant HCs in a cell-free system, which can be used to produce a trivalent HCA, HC B, HC E vaccine.
the development and production of botulinum vaccines in cell-free systems.
the development of a new generation of botulinum vaccines, in which the native Hc genes are used as the genetic source to produce the vaccine components in an in vitro system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a cell-free expression approach is a promising strategy for the production of a trivalent vaccine based on botulinum toxins Hc fragments.
the HcA, B, and Es are effective antigens in a cell-free system, and that the HcE protein is a better antigen than HcA and HcB.
the in vitro expression of the Hc fragments of the botulinum toxin A, B, or E, using a cell-free protein expression system, is a viable alternative for the preparation of a vaccine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hc fragment is a suitable candidate to be used as a component of a botulinum vaccine and that the in vitro expression system is a promising alternative to produce this vaccine.
we have shown that a vaccine based on Hc fragments of botulinum toxin A, B, or E can be produced in a cell-free system, and that it can be used to protect against botulinum intoxication.
a trivalent HCA/B/E botulinum vaccine was prepared using a novel cell-free expression system that produced the recombinant heavy chain proteins in a soluble form.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of cell-free expression systems to produce recombinant Hcs of botulinum toxin is a viable approach for the production of a trivalent vaccine.
cell-free protein synthesis is a promising alternative for the production of recombinant Hcs.
a trivalent HCA, HcB and HcE cell-free produced vaccine is highly immunogenic and protective in mice against a high toxin challenge.
